seoTitle: How to Connect a GoDaddy Domain to Google Workspace
metaDescription: Learn how to connect your GoDaddy domain to Google Workspace and set up Gmail with a branded email address in 2026, including DNS records.
intro: Using a GoDaddy-registered domain with Gmail lets you send and receive email from a professional address like you@yourdomain.com. This guide covers verifying your domain and adding the right DNS records in GoDaddy to activate Gmail through Google Workspace.

steps.heading: Sign in to your Admin Console
steps.body: Start from the Google Workspace Admin Console, where you'll verify your GoDaddy domain before adding DNS records.

steps.heading: Verify your domain from GoDaddy
steps.body: Google provides a verification code or TXT record that you'll add in your GoDaddy DNS settings to prove domain ownership.

steps.heading: Add MX records in GoDaddy DNS
steps.body: Log in to GoDaddy's DNS management and enter the MX records Google provides, replacing any conflicting records from a previous email provider.

steps.heading: Set up SPF, DKIM, and TXT records
steps.body: Beyond MX records, add the recommended SPF, DKIM, and TXT records to improve email deliverability and reduce the chance of messages landing in spam.

steps.heading: Test that Gmail is working
steps.body: Send a test email to and from your new domain address to confirm everything is routing correctly after DNS propagation.

faq.question: How long does it take for GoDaddy DNS changes to activate Gmail?
faq.answer: DNS propagation can take anywhere from a few minutes to 48 hours, so give it time before assuming something's wrong.

faq.question: Do I need to remove my old GoDaddy email records first?
faq.answer: Yes, existing MX records from a previous email service should be removed or replaced to avoid delivery conflicts with Google Workspace.

faq.question: Why isn't my email working after adding the MX records?
faq.answer: Double-check that the records match Google's exact values and priorities, and confirm there aren't leftover conflicting records still active.

faq.question: Are SPF and DKIM records required or optional?
faq.answer: They're technically optional but strongly recommended, since they significantly improve email deliverability and reduce the chance of your mail being flagged as spam.
